title: Measured HCN2 hyperpolarization in vivo was about half the model's prediction

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Measured HCN2 hyperpolarization in vivo was about half the model's prediction

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Hcn2 mRNA injection hyperpolarized the neural Vmem signal of Xenopus embryos by about 15 mV relative to controls, whereas the BETSE model predicted about 30 mV.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 corrects Vmem

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: However, the extent of enhanced hyperpolarization predicted by BETSE model for IT and HCN2 was higher (~30 mV) than actually observed (~15 mV) (Figs. 3e and 4).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › HCN2 corrects Vmem”. Scope: Xenopus laevis neurula-stage embryos injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claimed discrepancy is numerically precise and the simulation can be rerun. The in-vivo estimate cannot be fully audited without embryo-level calibrated imaging or recordings, so present resources resolve only part of the comparison.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate the injected-versus-control neural Vmem difference from embryo-level calibrated measurements and reproduce the matching model condition, then test whether observed and predicted effects are near 15 and 30 mV respectively.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The model side is more reproducible than the in-vivo side.

Raw voltage measurements are not linked to an open repository.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.97
data adequacy: 0.38
analysis feasibility: 0.86
data existence: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both sides of the comparison are quantitative. Only the simulated 30 mV can be regenerated from public code and the printed parameters. The embryo 15 mV is a published summary of images that were not deposited, so the discrepancy cannot be remeasured, only checked for consistency with the model. The claim is therefore half open.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare two deltas at the neural tube: simulated HCN2 (or IT) hyperpolarization versus control, and dye-calibrated in vivo hyperpolarization after Hcn2 mRNA. The discrepancy claim holds if the model delta is near 30 mV and the embryo delta near 15 mV; either number moving onto the other would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The in vivo ~15 mV comes from non-public voltage-dye images.

Model millivolts move with the reconstructed cAMP and leak settings.

Dye calibration depends on a small set of whole-cell recordings.
